title: Data-driven Mixed Integer Optimization through Probabilistic Multi-variable Branching
claim: Across threshold values, the quality bounds and set sizes shift predictably, with a sweet spot near 0.9 that justifies the chosen threshold.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared x-axis, green dashed vertical line
description: Three side-by-side line plots share the same x-axis, the threshold tau, running from 0.5 to 1.0. Each panel has a green dashed vertical line at about tau=0.9. The left panel plots the mean of accuracies. The blue alpha_U curve and the orange alpha_L curve rise gently, and a red diagonal line for tau crosses them near 0.9. The middle panel plots the variance of accuracies. Both curves decline, with blue alpha_U well above orange alpha_L. The right panel plots the number of variables. Orange L(tau) sits above blue U(tau), and both fall as tau grows. Blue, orange and red lines on white backgrounds with gray gridlines. The eye goes first to the green dashed line and the crossing point in the left panel.
caption: The mean and variance of αL(τ; ξ) and αU(τ; ξ), along with the average sizes of L(τ; ξ) and U(τ; ξ), computed over 100 independent set instances for varying values of the threshold parameter τ.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Pre-trained Mixed Integer Optimization framework (PreMIO) that accelerates online mixed integer program (MIP) solving with offline datasets and machine learning models. Our method is based on a data-driven multi-variable cardinality branching procedure that splits the MIP feasible region using hyperplanes chosen by the concentration inequalities. Unlike most previous ML+MIP approaches that either require complicated implementation or suffer from a lack of theoretical justification, our method is simple, flexible, provable, and explainable. Numerical experiments on both classical OR benchmark datasets and real-life instances validate the efficiency of our proposed method.
